item.title: CAUGHT WITH CASH: Fake “friend” fare ends with private hire driver arrested for plying-for-hire after £30 sting
item.description: Image credit: PC Patrick Quinton / Avon and Somerset Police A private hire vehicle driver has been arrested in Bristol after being caught illegally plying-for-hire during an early-morning police operation, according to Avon and Somerset Police. item.title: ON THE RISE: London City Airport to introduce £8 drop-off charge from 6 January 2026
item.description: Image credit: London City Airport London City Airport will introduce a new drop-off charge for vehicles using its forecourt from 6 January 2026, becoming the latest UK airport to monetise short dwell times at terminal kerbsides. Under the new structure, drivers will be charged £8 for stays of up to five minutes. After that, a £1 per minute fee will apply, with a maximum permitted stay of ten minutes. Blue Badge holders will be exempt from the charge. The airport said the move is intended to...

item.title: London cabbies warn fellow taxi drivers over latest distraction thefts hitting St Pancras Eurostar set-down
item.description: Taxi drivers are warning fellow cabbies to be on heightened alert at the St Pancras Eurostar set-down area following a reported theft incident involving distraction tactics during the morning peak. According to an account shared within the trade, the incident occurred at around 9.30am when a licensed taxi dropped passengers at the Eurostar entrance at St Pancras International. item.title: Blackburn with Darwen set to retain council-only MOT testing for taxis and private hire vehicles
item.description: A report to the Executive Board of Blackburn with Darwin Borough Council recommends no change to existing MOT testing arrangements for taxis licensed in the borough, keeping testing restricted to the council’s own vehicle testing facility. Under the current system, licensed taxi drivers are required to use the council’s Motor Vehicle Service Station at Davyfield Road for all MOT tests. item.title: CROSS-BORDER REFORM: Cambridgeshire and Peterborough Mayor backs shift of taxi licensing powers to mayoral authorities
item.description: The Mayor of Cambridgeshire and Peterborough, Paul Bristow, has called for taxi and private hire vehicle licensing powers to be transferred from local councils to mayoral combined authorities, arguing the existing framework is no longer fit for purpose and is driving standards down. item.description: Image credit: Blaby District Council A joint taxi enforcement operation between Blaby District Council and City of Wolverhampton Council has resulted in multiple vehicles failing safety and compliance checks during a coordinated inspection exercise in Leicestershire. item.title: London black cab fleet stabilises as retirements slow and Knowledge numbers rise
item.description: London’s black cab fleet remains below the 14,000 vehicle mark but is showing signs of stabilisation, according to the latest figures and commentary published in the Licensed Taxi Drivers’ Association’s (LTDA) trade newspaper. item.title: “CALCULATING SEXUAL PREDATORS”: Taxi driver and other man jailed for rape of vulnerable woman at Bristol guest house
item.description: Image credit: Avon & Somerset Police Two men described in court as calculating sexual predators have been jailed after being convicted of raping a vulnerable woman at a guest house in Bristol six years ago. item.description: Image credit: Sherbet Sherbet has confirmed that Lee Drinkwater, a founding partner and long-standing senior figure in its fleet operations, has stepped back from day-to-day involvement in the business, marking the end of a significant chapter in the company’s development. item.title: FROM BURNOUT TO BALANCE: Managing stress behind the wheel in the taxi trade
item.description: Taxi driving is often sold quite rightly as flexible, independent work. But like any job, it can be mentally and physically draining at times. Long hours, traffic congestion, difficult passengers, changes in demand and constant vigilance behind the wheel all add up. Many drivers accept stress as part of the job, but unmanaged pressure has a habit of creeping into health, relationships and decision making.
